text:
Devin: heads-up — perf triage on host-side for small streaming requests. p95/p99 CPU for 1-16 token responses spiked ~30% after last kernel selector change. seeing overhead in tokenization + socket path (small writes).
Anya: yikes. is this the kernel selection rollout? which workload?
Devin: yes, rolled kernel-v2 for better decode throughput. heavy in batch workloads but microbench shows host-prep path regressed for tiny responses (chat streaming).
Mike: can you paste the flame?
Devin: pasted short excerpt from perf
```
perf top --sort=cpu -n 50
  tokenize_host.cpp:parse_tokens      38.6%
  http2_stream.cpp:recv_frame         20.1%
  socket_writer.cpp:writev            12.4%
  kv_cache_lookup                      6.9%
  kernel_selector::choose              4.2%
```
Devin: also saw more syscalls in tail path — small writev calls instead of coalesced slab writes.  p99 latency up ~15ms for ~8-token responses.
Helen: hmm. kernel change probably shifted CPU affinity leading to more context switches on host threads reading input frames. Did you check batching heuristics? maybe min-batch-ms got lowered?
Devin: batching config unchanged, but the new kernel prefers continuous prefetch which increases preparse time per-request in low-batch scenarios. suggests we need to add more aggressive request coalescing at ingress.
Anya: can infra-bot run the wiring check for writev coalescing metrics? I want counts for small-write fragments.
infra-bot: running ingress/io-metrics query... (results attached)
infra-bot: 
```
ingress_small_write_count: 13242
ingress_coalesced_write_count: 2843
avg_frag_per_write: 1.9
avg_write_size_bytes: 312
```
Anya: avg_frag_per_write < 2 — that's bad for throughput. writev isn't being used effectively.
Mike: hypothesis: tokenization now emits more frequent flushes because token boundaries changed with new kernel hints. need to check tokenizer flush policy and streaming chunker behavior.
Devin: confirmed: tokenizer now outputs smaller chunks (~50-150 bytes) vs previous (~200-400 bytes). small chunks + http2 HEADERS/CONTINUATION frames -> extra syscalls.
Helen: possible quick mitigation: enable ingress small_write_coalesce (user-space aggregator) and bump window for stream-assembler to hold >1 chunk before flush for low latency tier. tradeoffs: adds ~1-2ms for first byte in some cases but reduces syscall overhead massively.
Anya: can we test toggling this on canary? also check KV cache effect — if kv lookups are slower, host prep can't overlap well with kernel decode.
Devin: KV doesn't look bad in this trace but there is a small bump in kv-miss handling. leaving note to profile kv cache hotpath with cpu sampling.
Mike: quick reproduce steps I used locally:
```bash
# run small-stream benchmark
cargo run --release --bin ingress-bench -- --clients 100 --req-size 8 --stream 1 --duration 120
# capture perf
sudo perf record -F 99 -g -- ./target/release/ingress-bench
sudo perf script | flamegraph.pl > flame.svg
```
Mike: when I flip `ingress.small_write_coalesce = true` locally, write syscalls drop ~75% and p99 improves by ~9ms.
Devin: nice. can we add a kernel-selection guard: if avg_response_tokens < 32 and avg_write_size_bytes < 500 then prefer kernel-v1 for host-affinity? avoids hitting the regressed path for small chat.
Helen: love that — a routing policy based on request shape. we can implement as a smart routing rule in smart-routing layer. low-risk.
Anya: action items:
- (Devin) open a canary to enable small_write_coalesce and stream-assembler hold on host canary pool.
- (Mike) add a micro-benchmark comparing kernel-v1 vs kernel-v2 for <32 token responses. include syscalls and p99.
- (Helen) prototype routing rule for short-response affinity to kernel-v1.
- (Infra) collect kv hotpath sampling for next run.
Devin: created a quick ticket `ENG-rt/ingress-small-write-coalesce-canary` and added notes. I'll post canary results in this thread. cc @Anya @Mike. :thumbsup:
Anya: thanks. if canary looks good let's ship a temporary guard while we iterate on kernel selector.
Mike: agree. also let's add a tight metric: small_write_ratio and syscalls_per_request to the runtime dashboard.
Devin: adding dashboard panels now. will follow up with numbers.
Helen: if we need to revert kernel-v2 for canary hosts, coordinate with releases channel — low-risk revert should be quick.
Devin: noted. thanks all.
